abstract: Small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs) are a large, evolutionarily conserved family of non-coding RNAs that guide ribosomal RNA (rRNA) modifications. Recent years have seen growing interest in the biological and biomedical roles of snoRNAs, their guided rRNA modifications, and their alternative functions. snoDB is a specialized database that aggregates human snoRNA annotations and features, including genomic location, host gene, conserved motifs, protein and RNA interactors, expression levels, as well as rRNA target sites and modification levels. In this third release, we expand the database to include murine snoRNAs with an equivalent level of annotation, update human snoRNA host genes, RNA interactors and protein interactors, and introduce new tools to establish snoRNA and rRNA target cross-species correspondence. snoDB 3.0 is available at https://bioinfo-scottgroup.med.usherbrooke.ca/snoDB/.
